source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC Web UI -> Click "Sensor" from the menu bar.
2. Click "Sensor detail" to check each sensor. Send command: ipmitool sdr elist
3. Jam FAN by a cable ties and check BMC SEL and health LED.
4. Recover and check the FAN status.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Sensor value should be OK in the reasonable range.
2. Sensor value is same as ipmi sdr command and web ui
3. BMC should record the error message and health LED shoule be amber when trigger error.
4. FAN status should recover after remove the cable ties.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Jam System FAN 1~N Status: jamming a physical fan (1~N) to force a failed-FAN SEL/behaviour requires a person physically stopping the fan rotor. Agent cannot jam a fan over SSH.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator stops the fan and captures the SEL/behaviour (alarm, LED); agent cannot produce this physically.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: jamming a fan can overheat the system or damage the motor; physical human action only.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly protects the physical fan-stop boundary and identifies overheating/motor damage, but it overlooks that mapped WebUI/IPMI/SEL, peer-fan response, temperatures and recovery can be collected automatically after package and operator approval.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly treats the case as hybrid, requires an actual FAN1~N map, approved fixture and bounded monitoring rather than blocking solely on physical action.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 807/2291 repeats NO and source Criteria but does not define cooling zones, phase-specific ranges, safe fixture, compensation response or evidence recovery.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-972 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently adds fan-module/zone identity, peer-fan compensation, critical-component thermal margin, rotor-current/mechanical inspection and explicit coverage limits for tach injection.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves the actual fan-failure stimulus and recovery rather than substituting a read-only default, ED-36 treats mapping/limits/fixture as readiness inputs, and ED-38 keeps physical actions, visual observations and verdicts engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: For every fitted and applicable system FAN1~N, create a bounded physical rotor-stall or approved equivalent fault, prove the correct mapped WebUI/IPMI status, BMC event and amber health indication plus expected cooling-zone compensation, then release the fault and prove mechanical, thermal and status recovery.
original_method: Use BMC WebUI Sensor detail and `ipmitool sdr elist`, physically jam one system fan with a cable tie, inspect SEL and the chassis health LED, then remove the tie and check fan recovery. The cable-tie text remains preserved but requires an approved non-damaging fixture before execution.
manual_activity: A qualified operator identifies the physical fan/module, installs and releases the approved fixture without reaching blades or energized internals, observes rotation and the amber chassis LED, and inspects the fan after recovery. Automation may collect mapped sensor, SEL, peer-fan, temperature and host evidence.
required_inputs: Actual fitted fan count N and per-fan physical slot/module/FRU, connector/controller channel, cooling zone, airflow role, RPM/PWM/status SDR and WebUI identity
Vendor qualification or service procedure for a reversible stall/fault, approved non-conductive fixture and access point, maximum stall duration, release and post-test inspection
Per-phase Expected Values for baseline RPM/range, stalled RPM/status, debounce/latency, SEL assert/deassert, amber LED, peer-fan compensation and recovery timeout
System workload, fan/zone redundancy, component thermal margins and independent inlet/CPU/GPU/DIMM/VR/drive temperature abort limits
Protected BMC access, ipmitool/WebUI versions, evidence timestamps, attended operator and emergency release/recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not use an improvised cable tie against a spinning rotor, reach through a guard, introduce loose material or obstruct a fan not explicitly approved for the fixture.
Confirm the target fan/zone and remaining cooling capacity under the actual workload; lower load only through the approved plan and record the changed coverage.

Use independent zone and critical-component temperatures plus target/peer RPM monitoring; bound the stall and release immediately on rapid thermal rise, peer-fan failure, unexpected shutdown, vibration/noise or wrong sensor transition.
Do not let BMC polling be the sole safety control, because a local hotspot or stalled-motor current can develop between updates.
Export baseline logs before any approved clear, preserve the first event, and never automatically retry a stall or move to the next fan after an anomaly.

Test one fan at a time; after release prove free rotation, commanded/actual RPM, peer-fan normalization, zone temperatures, BMC status, SEL deassertion, health LED and host stability before continuing.
Stop and quarantine the fan/module on damaged blades, bearings, connector, guard, retained fixture material, abnormal current/noise or incomplete recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate the fan map, fixture, thermal envelope and package without any DUT change.
After approval, collect same-identity WebUI and IPMI readings with timestamps plus target/peer RPM/PWM, zone/component temperatures, SEL, BMC health and host continuity around the engineer stimulus.
Separate baseline-normal, stall-fault/compensation and recovery-normal criteria; `reasonable range` cannot mean the same RPM/status during all phases.
Do not touch a rotor/fixture, alter fan policy/PWM, claim physical LED or rotation evidence, clear logs, retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the applicable population, physical/SDR/zone map, fixture or equivalent stimulus, state/event matrix, workload/thermal envelope, duration, abort and recovery.
Apply/release the physical fault, observe rotor and amber LED, supervise independent temperatures and immediately stop on limits.
Inspect the fan/module, verify full cooling and telemetry recovery and issue per-fan plus overall DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its operator-only stall description tests the right physical purpose, but NO is too coarse because the source explicitly requires WebUI/IPMI/SEL comparison and recovery evidence that can be automated after approval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After package validation, retain the concise engineer-controlled one-fan stall/release procedure and collect mapped `ipmitool sdr elist`, WebUI, SEL, target/peer fan and zone-temperature evidence with protected authentication.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: System FAN1~N, WebUI Sensor detail, `ipmitool sdr elist`, cable-tie wording, SEL, amber health LED, recovery, no Script and 5/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONDITIONAL ON FIXTURE, MAP AND APPROVAL
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map one system fan and its cooling zone at a time, baseline target/peer cooling, apply an approved bounded reversible stall, correlate RPM/status/SEL/LED and peer compensation under independent thermal monitoring, release immediately and prove complete mechanical/thermal/status recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact chassis fan population, module/zone/redundancy design, controller/BMC mapping and workload envelope.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/fan FRU, BMC/SDR/fan-controller/CPLD firmware and ipmitool/WebUI versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor fan-fault qualification, fan-module service, cooling-zone redundancy, thermal-limit and BMC event/LED specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains real system-fan failure coverage but replaces an ad hoc tie with an approved reversible fixture and adds zone/peer compensation and hardware inspection evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tach disconnect or BMC fault injection may validate monitoring, SEL, LED and control response but cannot automatically prove stalled-rotor current, airflow loss, local thermals or mechanical recovery; omitted physical paths must be declared.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Fan/zone map, fixture or equivalent-method approval, state/event matrix, thermal envelope and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The impact depends on cooling-zone topology: stopping a seemingly redundant fan can strand a local component even when aggregate chassis airflow remains high.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve controller/tach injection or a removable fan-module method only with a documented equivalence map for detection, compensation, airflow/thermal and recovery; it must retain the original physical-stall obligation and state any untested path.
expected_evidence: Fitted FAN1~N physical slot/module/FRU/controller/zone/RPM/PWM/SDR/WebUI applicability map and approved event matrix
Vendor fixture/access approval, duration/release SOP, workload/cooling margin, independent abort limits and operator record
Per-fan baseline target/peer RPM/PWM, zone and critical-component temperatures, UI/IPMI status, SEL, BMC health and chassis LED
Stall/release timestamps, physical target identity, target fault transition, peer compensation, thermal/host timeline, SEL assert and engineer-observed amber LED
Recovered free rotation, commanded/actual RPM, peer normalization, temperatures, status, SEL deassertion, health LED and host health plus physical inspection
Per-fan coverage/override disclosure, unexpected-event review and engineer-owned verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target a system-fan stall, mapped UI/IPMI observation, BMC/LED response and recovery. N, `reasonable range`, fixture and timing are Project readiness inputs; they do not create an irreconcilable target or acceptance contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The fan target class, physical stimulus and expected fault/recovery direction are identifiable. Exact population, limits and approved fixture are required before execution, but a hybrid operator-plus-automation method is feasible and the Review is not permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes NO/manual-only to a package/user-confirmation hybrid while retaining its physical-action prohibition and overheating warning.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on the hybrid class and strengthens zone/peer-fan evidence, phase-specific ranges, motor/mechanical checks and alternate-stimulus coverage limits.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces physical-only handling with auditable automated evidence and explicit thermal recovery without automating the rotor action.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the package classification but adds per-zone failure analysis and separates monitoring-logic coverage from actual airflow/mechanical coverage.

review_improvement: Makes every applicable chassis fan independently accountable for detection, cooling compensation and full physical recovery without allowing unsafe improvised obstruction or a read-only substitute.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike a PSU-internal fan, a system fan's primary blast radius is its cooling zone and peer-control response. The stall and visual confirmation remain manual, but time-aligned RPM, sensor, SEL, temperature and recovery collection is a material automatable core. Missing map and fixture data affect readiness rather than the intelligibility of the test.
